citation.quote: The recreational fishery for surfperch (PDF) (opens in new tab) (family Embiotocidae) is open year-round. The daily bag and possession limit is 20 fish in combination of all species (except shiner perch), with not more than 10 fish of any one species. Shiner perch ( Cymatogaster aggregata ) have a separate bag and possession limit of 20 fish. Redtail surfperch ( Amphistichus rhodoterus ) have a minimum size limit of 10½ inches total length.

californiaHalibut.basis: Section "California Halibut": season, bag south of Point Sur, minimum length.

citation.quote: The recreational fishery for California halibut ( Paralichthys californicus ) remains open year-round. The daily bag and total possession limit is five fish south of Point Sur, Monterey County. The minimum size limit is 22 inches total length.

m2EsteroBluffs.basis: The fetched NOAA layer lists original objects around the four access points (below), mostly 1A/2A rocky and 5 mixed sand and gravel classes with composite codes; this card does not choose a run, bounds or substrate rule. Choosing among them needs the M2 schema decision and owner review, and an automatic nearest-shore join is not allowed.
m2EsteroBluffs.listingRule: Every layer object with any vertex inside the access points bounding box padded by 0.02 degrees; a listing, not a selection.
m2EsteroBluffs.legendSource: pages/noaa-layer3-metadata.json drawingInfo.renderer (field MOSTSENSIT); a composite ESI code has no own legend entry, each part is listed with its code legend where one exists.

siteSelectionLimits.basis: No bounded latitude/longitude window is proposed: none can be substantiated from the layer alone without inferring an extent.

ownerUrl.basis: The fetched sources carry no official owner page URL for Estero Bluffs State Park; none is guessed. A State Parks page is outside the three-source scope of this card.
